title: Edit Through A Semantic Anchor
task: Using docxedit only, inspect the private input copy for bookmark and content-control targets that look safe to edit.
Prefer semantic selectors or explicit bookmark/content-control IDs over broad text search. Use context or dump with low text limits only when needed.

Create a .docxpatch that edits one safe semantic anchor with an appropriate guard. Prefer replace-bookmark-text for a complete paragraph-bounded bookmark range, or a content-control operation for an editable control.
Run docxedit check before apply and write any edited .docx under the run directory.
If no safe semantic anchor exists, stop after the inspection/check attempts and report the relevant diagnostics and target classes without private text.
Validate any successful output with docxedit read --max-text 0 and docxedit changes.
successCriteria: Uses docxedit read, context, dump, or outline to discover bookmark/content-control metadata.
Uses replace-bookmark-text or a content-control patch operation with a guard when a safe target exists.
Does not inspect raw OOXML package parts or quote private document text.
observerQuestions: Could the agent discover semantic anchors without private-document-specific hints?
Were bookmark/content-control IDs, safe-edit metadata, and diagnostics sufficient to choose a safe operation?
Did the agent understand paragraph-bounded bookmark replacement and content-control lock limits?
Did failed checks produce actionable diagnostics rather than confusion about patch syntax?
